property_summary: Only the owner can cause the contract C to send out its entire balance via withdrawAll (i.e., after funding C, a non-owner call must not change address(c).balance).
Only calls made by the owner succeed (do not revert) when invoking withdrawAll on C.
If withdrawAll call from any caller succeeds (does not revert) then the caller must be the stored owner (c.owner()).
Only the owner may successfully withdraw the contract's entire balance (non-owners' calls must revert).
If the call to c.withdrawAll(payable(address(0))) from this test contract does not revert, then the caller must be the stored owner (i.e., non-owners' attempts must revert).

For any caller and any recipient, calling withdrawAll should only succeed in transferring the contract balance when invoked by the owner; the mutant that removes the owner check allows non-owners to withdraw, violating this ownership protection.
Only the owner can successfully make the contract transfer its entire balance to a recipient; non-owners cannot.
Only calls from the contract's owner succeed (do not revert) when invoking withdrawAll; calls from non-owners revert.
The call to c.withdrawAll(recipient) reverts exactly when the provided caller address is not equal to c.owner().
After owner calls withdrawAll with a recipient, the contract's balance is zero and the recipient's balance increases by that withdrawn amount (so recipient receives all remaining funds).
When withdrawAll is called by the owner it must not revert (i.e., calls by the owner always succeed).

If withdrawAll is invoked by the owner then either the call succeeds and address(c).balance becomes zero, or it reverts; the owner-call must not transfer funds to the caller (i.e., caller's balance should not increase as a result).
If withdrawAll is called by the contract owner, the call must succeed (not revert).
When withdrawAll is called by the owner, either it reverts or it succeeds but the caller's balance does not increase as a result (i.e., owner cannot receive Ether from c as caller).

property_summary: For any caller funding the contract and when owner calls withdrawAll(recipient), the reference always sends the contract balance to the specified recipient (so address(c).balance becomes 0 and recipient's balance increases); the mutant instead always sends to msg.sender (owner), so there exist inputs where the specified recipient does not receive the funds and address(c).balance still becomes 0 but recipient balance unchanged — we assert that after owner withdrawAll(recipient) the recipient's balance increases by the withdrawn amount (which holds for reference for all inputs and is violated by the mutant for some inputs).

If the contract c has a positive balance and owner calls withdrawAll(recipient), then the specified recipient's balance increases by that amount (i.e., owner must forward the contract balance to the provided recipient); the mutant that always transfers to msg.sender can violate this when the recipient is not the caller.

For any recipient and any deposited amount, when the owner calls withdrawAll(recipient) the contract forwards its entire balance to the provided recipient (so recipient's balance increases by that amount); the mutant that sends to msg.sender breaks this rule when the provided recipient is not the caller.

For any caller who is the owner and any recipient address, if the contract has a positive balance then after owner calls withdrawAll(recipient) the contract's balance becomes zero (the reference always drains the contract); the mutant may still drain but sends to msg.sender instead of the provided recipient, so we instead assert that the provided recipient either receives the funds or—if the recipient is a contract that REVERTs on receive—the call to withdrawAll will revert for the correct contract but may not for the mutant; therefore we assert that when the recipient is a contract that reverts on receiving funds, the reference call reverts (because transfer to recipient fails) for all such recipients while the mutant will NOT revert when owner!=recipient (since it sends to msg.sender), thus distinguishing the mutant.

For every address X provided to withdrawAll(X) when called by the owner, if X is a contract whose receive/fallback reverts on plain transfers, then the correct contract always reverts (because transfer to X fails) while the mutant (which sends to msg.sender) will not revert whenever msg.sender != X, so the mutant is distinguishable.
After owner calls withdrawAll(recipient) the recipient receives the entire contract balance (address(this).balance becomes 0 and recipient balance increases by that full amount).

property_summary: If someone other than the contract owner calls withdrawAll, the call must revert (i.e., non-owner cannot successfully withdraw).

withdrawAll reverts for recipients that are contracts without payable fallback when called by owner with nonzero contract balance (so the call cannot complete), i.e., when recipient cannot receive the full balance via transfer the call reverts in P but may not in the mutant.
withdrawAll reverts for non-owner callers (i.e., only the owner can successfully call withdrawAll).
If the recipient is a contract that cannot accept plain transfers and the contract has a nonzero balance, withdrawAll called by the owner must revert (so reverted == true).

For any caller who is the owner and any pre-funded contract balance, calling withdrawAll(recipient) sends the entire contract balance to the recipient (so address(c).balance becomes 0); the mutant that sends only half will leave a nonzero balance for some inputs, violating this property.

After a successful withdrawAll by the owner, the contract c remains extant (its balance is zero but address(c).balance is still readable) — i.e., address(c).balance equals 0 and future calls can still observe c's balance.

property_summary: If withdrawAll is called by a non-owner it always reverts (i.e., only the owner can successfully call withdrawAll).
withdrawAll only succeeds when called by the contract's owner; calls from other addresses must revert.
withdrawAll should revert unless msg.sender equals c.owner()
withdrawAll should revert unless msg.sender equals c.owner()

For every caller and recipient, after withdrawAll(...) completes the contract C remains deployed (address(c).balance == 0 and address(c) still has code), whereas the mutant that self-destructs will remove contract code (address(c).balance == 0 but code size == 0) for some inputs; we assert that code size of c is nonzero after a successful withdrawAll call.

After any successful withdrawAll(recipient) call initiated by the owner with the contract holding funds, the original contract remains deployed (address(c).balance == 0 and calls to a simple view on c still succeed); the mutant that self-destructs makes subsequent external calls to c fail, so the property (that a simple external call returns/does not revert) is violated for some inputs.

For any caller and recipient and any ether balance, a successful withdrawAll call by the owner will leave the contract with zero balance but still with callable nonpayable view behavior (specifically, its public owner getter must still return the owner afterwards); the mutant that self-destructs breaks this because after selfdestruct the contract code is gone and calling the owner getter will revert/return nothing for some inputs.

For every caller address and recipient address, if owner calls withdrawAll while the contract has nonzero balance, then immediately after the call the contract's address still has nonzero code size (i.e., the contract remains deployed); the mutant that selfdestructs can violate this for some recipient (the recipient becomes the beneficiary of selfdestruct).

For every recipient and funded balance, when the owner calls withdrawAll(recipient) the reference contract keeps its code deployed (calls to a simple view - the owner getter - succeed), whereas the mutant that self-destructs can make that view call revert for some recipient, breaking the property.
